title: Live resource lookup became available after delayed initialization
observed: GameSettingsPresetsResource, BalancingTable, RecipeRegistryResource, WorkshopRegistryResource, and ItemInfo returned tables
conclusion: Bounded live resource lookup is available after world initialization.
next_steps: Run a bounded read-only field inventory against settings and balancing resources.

title: Guarded no-op appearance write accepted and restored
observed: Readback matched the original zero value
conclusion: The typed resource accessor accepted a reversible no-op write on a preset field, but this is not proof of live player editing.
next_steps: Test field ownership and visible effect separately under private-world safeguards.

title: Localization inventory was blocked by the EML export profile
observed: EML launch record reported exports disabled
conclusion: The failure is attributed to the active EML runtime/export profile, not to a completed negative localization capability test.
next_steps: Retain the probe for a compatible EML profile and repeat the export test.

title: Loader conflict report found entry-point collisions and repeated loads
conclusion: The report identifies environment-specific loader collisions and repeated events, but the unknown game-build field prevents build-scoped compatibility claims.
next_steps: Repeat on a clean, build-identified installation and separate active files from backups and pending updates.

title: Stage 1 build baseline recorded without a comparable predecessor
observed: No prior complete source-identified snapshot found
conclusion: The checkpoint establishes a provenance baseline, not a semantic build-change claim.
next_steps: Create a future dated diff with source hashes and field-level additions/removals.

title: Registry verification was retained as observed pending reconciliation
observed: Scope included API capability and resource type probes
conclusion: The evidence matrix correctly prevents registry status from outrunning current-session report evidence.
next_steps: Reconcile current-session evidence before promoting the matrix.

title: Lua-facing API surface was present while the native backend remained incomplete
observed: Runtime root, type registry, ECS registry, component lookup, function metadata, services, overrides, game asset lookup, settings, logging, and export APIs were present
conclusion: API presence was established, but registry/layout, storage types, game-thread ownership, and resource service were unavailable for operational work.
next_steps: Match the build-specific native backend/profile before interpreting API presence as usable capability.

title: Blueprint resources were readable at runtime while nested payload semantics remained opaque
observed: One blueprint item registry was readable
Debug names and snapping fields were present
Nested payloads remained opaque userdata or typed values
conclusion: Blueprint resources are a confirmed readable runtime surface, not a confirmed editing or persistence surface.
next_steps: Perform bounded field reads on the seven configs without attempting placement or terrain writes.

title: Building census reached blueprint resources but not live voxel components
observed: ECS field reads and asset lookup were callable
One voxel blueprint registry and seven configs were observed
Targeted live voxel and no-build-zone queries were empty
conclusion: Blueprint resources are the first confirmed readable building surface; live voxel ownership remains unresolved.
next_steps: Continue bounded blueprint reads while keeping placement, teardown, pickup, and terrain modification out of scope.

title: Full private-world probe rerun refreshed broad read-only evidence
observed: Localization tags were visible but text remained hash-referenced
Inventory/player schemas were visible without resolved owner or live item instances
conclusion: The rerun broadened current-session observations while preserving unresolved ownership, localization text, and write boundaries.
next_steps: Separate confounding EML patch state from clean probe runs and continue domain-specific tests.

title: Roadmap audit closed stages 0 through 3 for their defined scopes
observed: Provenance foundation, static census, private baseline/recovery, and offline provider foundation met their defined exit criteria
Stage 4 lacked final smoke and worker-contract tests
conclusion: The audit promotes only explicitly scoped stages and keeps later unresolved capabilities open.
next_steps: Complete Stage 4 tests, establish unique player/inventory identity for Stage 5, then reassess Stage 6.
